mentions.name: RF Monitoring System
mentions.description: This RF monitoring system identifies and correlates nearby Bluetooth/BLE/WiFi devices (e.g. linking a parked car to a named set of earbuds by MAC address), alerts on sudden cross-spectrum interference such as cheap jammers used to knock out WiFi cameras, alerts when known devices lose contact or leave the premises, and reviews device movement across a campus or neighborhood using multiple RF pods. It runs on low-power hardware like a Raspberry Pi, supports multiple RF sensors, provides a web UI, can publish events to an external security system, and is gaining an LLM interface so a non-technical operator can set policies and ask questions. It could be sold as an appliance system or a license for a DIY build.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I'm building an RF monitoring system.

It can tell you things like:

- The car that parked nearby last night coincided with "Chad's Galaxy Buds"  with MAC address aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff. The buds also drove by briefly the previous night.

- Alert on sudden cross-specturm interference (e.g. burglars using a cheap jammer to knock out WiFi cameras).

- Alert on known device contact loss (powered off / left premises).

- Review device movement across a campus/neighborhood (using multiple RF pods).

I have a working PoC. It can run on a low-power computer (e.g. RPi) supporting multiple RF sensors (BT/BLE/WiFi). Has a web UI. Can publish events to an external security system. Currently working on an LLM interface to make it easy for a non-technical operator to set policies and ask questions.
